attributes.title: Total requests
attributes.description: LLM API requests captured on the nginx proxy within the time range (llm-request-body-*; one doc per POST)

attributes.title: Total responses
attributes.description: response docs in llm-response-body-* within the time range — fewer than requests while streams are in flight or failed before the response was captured

attributes.title: Avg request time (s)
attributes.description: mean end-to-end request time over the proxy (request_time from the nginx access line, both body indices)

attributes.title: Total tokens
attributes.description: prompt + completion tokens served in range (usage fields of llm-response-body-*; streams without include_usage report no usage)

attributes.title: Latency over time
attributes.description: end-to-end request time (nginx request_time) — mean plus p50/p90/p99; long streaming agentic calls dominate the tail

attributes.title: Upstream response time by instance
attributes.description: time spent in the upstream llama-server instance (upstream_response_time) per upstream_addr ip:port — load-balancing health across 8001-8004

attributes.title: Errors (4xx/5xx) over time
attributes.description: proxied requests whose upstream returned 4xx/502 (upstream_status >= 400); 200 = healthy

attributes.title: Finish reasons over time
attributes.description: completion finish_reason of llm-response-body-* — tool_calls = the agent loop requested another round, stop = final answer

attributes.title: Request payload size
attributes.description: size of the OpenAI-compatible request body (request_body_bytes, llm-request-body-*) — grows with the agentic conversation history

attributes.title: Response payload size
attributes.description: reconstructed completion size (response_body_bytes) vs bytes actually sent over the wire (body_bytes_sent), llm-response-body-*

attributes.title: Context growth (messages)
attributes.description: messages per request (messages_count, llm-request-body-*) — the depth of the agentic conversation being replayed to the model

attributes.title: Tools per request
attributes.description: tools exposed per request (tools_count, llm-request-body-*) — a guardrail signal: the function set sent to the model is expected to stay stable

attributes.title: SSE chunks per response
attributes.description: SSE events per streamed response (chunk_count, llm-response-body-*; non-streaming responses report 0/none)

attributes.title: Completion token distribution
attributes.description: per-response completion tokens (usage_completion_tokens) — p50/p90/p99; most of the tokens go into tool-call payloads

attributes.title: LLM Body Metrics
attributes.description: Per-request workload metrics parsed from the LLM body indices (llm-request-body-*, llm-response-body-*): latency, upstream instance timing, errors, finish reasons, payload sizes, agentic context depth (messages/tools per request) and streaming volume. Complements the LLM Observability dashboard (which covers request/response rates and token totals). Instance = upstream_addr ip:port (llama-server 8001-8003 behind the per-agent vhosts ui-agent / code-swarm-agent / code-smith-agent.llm.lan).

attributes.title: Top 20 slowest requests
attributes.description: requests ranked by end-to-end request_time (llm-response-body-*, one row per request_id; request_id is the join key to the request doc). upstream = time in the llama-server instance; tokens = usage reported by the model

attributes.title: Request rate
attributes.description: requests per bucket (llm-request-body-*) — read together with Response rate: the gap is in-flight or lost requests

attributes.title: Response rate
attributes.description: responses per bucket (llm-response-body-*) — a response lands when the stream ends, long after its request

attributes.title: Latency by instance
attributes.description: end-to-end request_time per upstream instance (upstream_addr ip:port) — whether one llama-server is consistently slower

attributes.title: Proxy vs upstream time
attributes.description: total request_time vs time inside the upstream (upstream_response_time); the gap is nginx proxy/buffering overhead (body capture, SSE pass-through)

attributes.title: Error requests
attributes.description: requests whose upstream returned 4xx/5xx (upstream_status >= 400) with their request_id — open the id in LLM Body Logs (Discover) to read the payloads. status is the upstream response code

attributes.title: Completion cap (max_tokens)
attributes.description: max_tokens cap sent per request (llm-request-body-*) — the completion budget the client allows

attributes.title: LLM Request Traces
attributes.description: Per-request view over the LLM body indices. request_id joins the request doc (llm-request-body-*) with the response doc (llm-response-body-*) — one request can span minutes of streaming, so the slowest-request table is keyed on request_time. Request vs response rates expose in-flight/lost requests (the gap). Use the LLM Body Logs (Discover) search to open an individual request_id and read its full request/response payloads. Instance = upstream_addr ip:port (llama-server 8001-8003 behind the per-agent vhosts ui-agent / code-swarm-agent / code-smith-agent.llm.lan).

attributes.title: LLM Body Logs (Discover)
attributes.description: All LLM request + response body docs in one Discover view (llm-*-body-*). Filter request_id:<id> to pull the request doc and its response doc side by side — request_id is the join key the nginx lua capture stamps on both. Fields present on only one side render empty on the other doc type.
